subject.title: [Feature]: Standardize skill data directory convention (configPaths) under ~/.openclaw/

question: Should OpenClaw define a core per-skill writable data directory contract, route stateful skill behavior to plugin state/SQLite APIs, or leave this as ClawHub authoring guidance?
rationale: The request changes public skill authoring and durable storage semantics, and the repository policy points in different directions depending on whether the data is prompt-skill content, plugin runtime state, or a named file artifact.

options.title: Prefer plugin state for writable runtime data
options.body: Stateful capabilities should become code plugins using plugin-state/SQLite APIs, while prompt skills stay instruction bundles plus read-only support files unless a narrower need is proven.

options.title: Adopt a core skill-data contract
options.body: Define a public SKILL.md metadata field or placeholder, create the directory during install, and add docs/tests for fresh install and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Document ClawHub guidance only
options.body: Publish a convention for community skills without adding runtime creation or resolution support, accepting that authors remain responsible for directory setup.

recommendation.title: Prefer plugin state for writable runtime data
recommendation.body: Stateful capabilities should become code plugins using plugin-state/SQLite APIs, while prompt skills stay instruction bundles plus read-only support files unless a narrower need is proven.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans skill docs, runtime metadata, ClawHub boundaries, and core storage policy, where recent history points to steipete as the strongest routing candidate.
